decisions.critiqueFinding: CRITIQUE-2/3 [0] — The candidate `_case_statuses` regresses a valid-bash reformat the shipped helper handles: a `::warning::` wrapped onto two lines with a ` #<number>` on the continuation. Composing a PER-LINE comment stripper (`code()`/`_uncomment`) with a WHOLE-TEXT quote masker (`_mask_quoted`) is the defect. Remedy: either (a) mask first on the raw body then strip comments using the mask, or (b) reset `_mask_quoted`'s state at each newline.
decisions.reasoning:
THE REGRESSION IS REAL — I reproduced it (task item (b)) — BUT BOTH PROPOSED REMEDIES ARE WRONG, AND I MEASURED THAT TOO.

Reproduction: spliced into the real `_body()`, `bash -n` clean, real assertion invoked. Two-line form, closing quote AFTER the ` #120`:
  echo "::warning::the published account audit reads: the Tier-3 Routine
  has not published a usable result recently. See #120 for the history." ;;
  shipped -> PASS ; spec candidate -> FAIL ('the audit step's `case` has no closing `esac` outside a string and outside a nested `case`').
Control with the `#` removed: both PASS. So the `#` is the trigger, and the message blames the case block for damage done upstream.

PRECISION THE CRITIQUE MISSES: the regression needs the CLOSING QUOTE to fall after the `#` on the SAME line. I measured a three-line variant whose closing quote sits on a later line — the spec candidate PASSES it. The fixture must therefore be the two-line form specifically, or it does not discriminate.

REMEDY (b), per-line masking: MEASURED, STRICTLY WORSE. It reds all three wrapped shapes, including the one with no `#` at all — line 1's unterminated `"` masks the rest of line 1, and line 2's closing `"` masks the `;;` after it, so the arm terminator vanishes. REJECTED.

REMEDY (a) as literally worded ('mask FIRST on the raw body, then strip comments using the mask'): MEASURED, BROKEN. An apostrophe inside a comment — `# skills-evals' verdict vocabulary ...`, a construction this repo's prose uses constantly — opens a quote in the mask and corrupts everything downstream. Shipped PASSES that shape; mask-first FAILS it. REJECTED.

WHAT ACTUALLY WORKS is neither: ONE INTERLEAVED WALK in which `#` is tested before quote state is entered, producing `text` and `mask` that are BOTH the same length as the raw body. Measured over 23 valid `bash -n`-clean reformats plus 4 negative controls plus the real body: 23/23 PASS (shipped reds 11 of them), 4/4 negative controls still red, real body PASS. Same-length output also preserves index mapping into `body`, which the spec's `code()`-based design destroys.
decisions.effectOnPlan: The whole FINDING 2 implementation is respecified around `_shell_scan(body) -> (text, mask)`, both the same length as `body` (EDIT 2.1). This also answers the critique's openQuestion 1 without its stated blast radius: `code()` is NOT touched, so TestTheCommentStripperTheseAssertionsRestOn and the eleven assertions resting on `code()` are unaffected. Three fixtures go into `_ARMS_OK` from this finding: the discriminating two-line wrapped-`#` form, the wrapped form with no `#`, and the wrapped form whose quote closes on a later line. A fourth, an apostrophe inside a comment, guards against the mask-first remedy being re-derived.
